spec_match.rationale: Exercises the real ML-DSA-44/65/87 generateKey/sign/verify surface plus the spec's new getPublicKey(privateKey) derivation and raw-public export, matching FIPS 204 and the chromestatus parameter-set list.

interactive.rationale: Parameter-set select, editable message textarea, sign and verify buttons, and a tamper checkbox that flips a bit before verification — a genuine sign/verify/negative-path loop with live signature sizes.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises sign/verify, tamper-to-fail, size comparison across the three sets, and getPublicKey(); all four are on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported browsers get the honest flag note and warn status, verification distinguishes tampered-invalid (correct) from untampered-invalid (error), exportKey falls back gracefully, and telemetry asserts the ok===!tamper contract.

references.rationale: See-also links siblings only — no direct https://chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 link anywhere on the page, weakening the per-page self-heal contract (all five webcrypto concepts share this gap).

conformance.rationale: The suite's getpublickey typeof and secure-context assertions cover this page's contract; the 7 failures in this unflagged Chromium 141 session are the expected absent WebCryptoPQC surface, not demo defects.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): initial DOM shows the visible flag note and honest warn status with sign enabled/verify disabled, zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; sign/verify/tamper interactions could not be driven non-interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts sign success with signature byte size, sign failures with error name, and the verify contract (valid iff untampered).

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, but the default-visible warn status (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1) and the flagged-path VALID verdict (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald, ~4.0:1) miss WCAG AA 4.5:1 at their small bold sizes.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled select and textarea, a native checkbox with a text label, role=status aria-live status line, aria-live signature cell, and verdicts written as text (VALID/INVALID) rather than colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (hex rows word-break, control row wraps); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus feature link to this page's see-also
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires every page to embed the chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 link as the slug self-heal anchor; this page links siblings only. One-line additive fix shared with the other four webcrypto concepts.

openQuestions.title: Fix sub-AA contrast on the warn status and VALID verdict
openQuestions.detail: status-line.warn (--accent-amber on --bg-stone) is the default visible state in unflagged browsers at ~3.5:1, and verdict.ok (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald) is ~4.0:1 — both under the 4.5:1 AA bar for 0.78–0.8rem bold text. Using --text-black on emerald (5.1:1) and a darker amber resolves it corpus-wide.

openQuestions.title: Record flagged-browser evidence of the size comparison across all three parameter sets
openQuestions.detail: The page's headline size trade-off (2420/3309/4627-byte signatures for ML-DSA-44/65/87) could not be observed in this unflagged Chromium 141. In a WebCryptoPQC-enabled Chrome 150+, sign with each set and capture the reported byte sizes plus a tampered-verify failure as evidence.

summary: Solid post-quantum signature demo covering sign, verify, single-bit tamper rejection, getPublicKey() derivation, and cross-set signature sizes, with an honest unsupported fallback. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): honest warn state, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either device class. Open items: per-page chromestatus link, amber/emerald AA contrast, and flagged-browser success evidence.
